items.title: Japan's Favourite?

question.text: Which sport has a huge modern spectator following in Japan?

choices.response: Yes. Night games and packed stands.
Sumo is famous. Check which fills TV most weeks.
Rugby has big moments. Look at the weekly crowds.
Judo is a Japanese gift to the Olympics. Look at spectators.

items.reveal: Baseball is one of Japan’s most watched sports.
items.notes: Do not say ‘the most popular’ as a hard fact until checked.

question.text: Which sport is commonly described as Japan’s national sport?

choices.response: Huge crowds. The ‘national’ label is usually used elsewhere.
Yes. That is the usual phrase.
Karate travelled the world from here. Check the national label.
Judo is a Japanese art. Check the national label.

moreInfo.title: Sumo and shrine
moreInfo.text: Sumo is tied to Shinto ritual: salt, the ring, the clap. Confirm whether ‘national sport’ is official or just a common phrase.

items.title: Made in Japan
items.task: Find five Japanese brands while walking around Tokyo.
items.hint: Nintendo, Sony, Uniqlo, Muji, Toyota, Canon, Casio, Asics.

items.title: Japan or Not?
items.task: Look at the marks. Talk through which ones are Japanese.

question.text: Which of these is not a Japanese brand?

choices.response: Japanese. Try a mark from elsewhere.
Yes. That one is not Japanese.
Also not Japanese. Samsung is the sample answer.

items.reveal: Nintendo, Sony, Muji and Uniqlo are Japanese. Samsung and Xiaomi are not.
items.visualIdea: Brand logo grid. Do not copy marks into git until license is clear.
items.notes: Single-choice stand-in for a multi-select logo grid. Xiaomi is a second non-Japanese mark.
